Join us in building the future of finance.

Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading.

About the team + role

We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world's biggest financial problems. We're looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn't a place for complacency, it's where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We're a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards.

Robinhood Derivatives, LLC (RHD) is Robinhood's CFTC-regulated futures commission merchant and NFA member, offering customers access to futures, options on futures, and event contracts. The RHD Compliance team is small, hands-on, and in build mode. We partner with Legal, Risk, Operations, Product, and Engineering to launch new derivatives products the right way, with clear regulations helping us build, innovate, and scale with confidence.

As the Futures Compliance Senior Specialist, you will directly report to the Chief Compliance Officer of RHD and be a core member of the team. You will help run and strengthen the day-to-day compliance program for our futures business, from policies and supervision to product reviews, marketing approvals, and regulatory interactions. This is a hands-on role for someone who knows futures regulation well and wants to help shape a program as the business grows.

This role is based in our Chicago, IL office , with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week.

What you’ll do

  • Support the design, operation, and ongoing testing of the RHD compliance program under the Commodity Exchange Act, CFTC regulations, and NFA rules
  • Draft, update, and maintain Written Supervisory Procedures (WSPs), policies, and internal controls as products, rules, and business processes change
  • Advise Product, Engineering, Operations, and Legal on the regulatory requirements for new and existing futures, options on futures, and event contract offerings, including customer-facing flows and disclosures
  • Review and approve marketing, social media, and other communications for compliance with NFA and CFTC standards, working through our Red Oak review workflow
  • Complete regulatory and exchange responses, including timely, accurate responses to NFA, CFTC, exchange, and clearing firm examinations, inquiries, and document requests, and track remediation of any findings through to closure
  • Handle the registration process for Associated Persons (APs), including Series 3 testing and registration and the filing of NFA Forms 8-R (registration) and 8-T (termination) in NFA's Online Registration System, and keep AP registration records current
  • Respond to 4g requests
  • Support regulatory filings and recurring obligations, including the NFA annual self-examination and required notices and reports
  • Support the firm's risk management program requirements under CFTC Regulation 1.11, and contribute to compliance monitoring, testing, and reporting to senior management
  • Review and escalate trade surveillance and monitoring alerts, working with Risk, Trading, and Operations to investigate and document outcomes
  • Own the customer complaint adjudication process for the futures business, from intake and investigation through resolution, documentation, and trend reporting
  • Support KYC and customer onboarding processes as they relate to the futures business
  • Track CFTC, NFA, and exchange rule changes and industry developments, and translate them into clear, practical guidance for the business
  • Contribute to the annual CCO report, Board reporting, and compliance training for RHD personnel

What you bring

  • 3-5 years of compliance experience in financial services, with direct experience in futures and derivatives at an FCM, introducing broker, exchange, clearing firm, or regulator (NFA or CFTC)
  • Active NFA Series 3 (National Commodity Futures Examination) is not required, but a nice-to-have. Ability to obtain it within 90 days of hire is required.
  • Working knowledge of the Commodity Exchange Act, CFTC regulations, and NFA rules, including supervision requirements (such as NFA Compliance Rule 2-9) and communications and promotional material standards
  • Experience supporting regulatory examinations, document requests, and responses to findings
  • Experience drafting and maintaining WSPs, policies, and compliance procedures
  • Ability to read complex rules, form a clear view, and give practical, well-documented guidance to product, engineering, and business partners who move fast
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with sound judgment and high attention to detail

What we offer

  • Challenging, high-impact work to grow your career
  • Performance driven compensation with multipliers for outsized impact, bonus programs, equity ownership, and 401(k) matching
  • Top Tier benefits to fuel your work, including 100% paid health insurance for employees with 90% coverage for dependents
  • Access to the best AI tools on the market and continuous AI skill-building for every employee, technical or not
  • Lifestyle wallet - a highly flexible benefits spending account for wellness, learning, and more
  • Employer-paid life & disability insurance, fertility benefits, and mental health benefits
  • Time off to recharge including company holidays, paid time off, sick time, parental leave, and more!
  • Exceptional office experience with catered meals, events, and comfortable workspaces.

Building the Future of Open Finance

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.

The team

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

Kraken’s world-class Security Team is growing. As we continue to scale and mature our information technology controls program, we are seeking a senior professional with a strong background in risk management to help build and operate a program designed for enterprise scale.

Kraken is seeking a Senior Risk Analyst to join the Security Governance, Risk, and Compliance (SecGRC) team. Reporting to the Senior Manager of Security Risk Management, this role is a key contributor to the execution and maturation of Kraken's Security Risk Management program. You'll conduct rigorous risk assessments, produce high-quality analysis, and help build the operational infrastructure that makes the program run — all in close partnership with program leadership. This role offers the opportunity to make a meaningful and lasting impact both within Kraken and across the broader industry.

The ideal candidate is deeply analytical, process-minded, and energized by turning ambiguous risk signals into clear, repeatable, and scalable workflows. Entrepreneurial spirit and comfort with iterating quickly is a must. This is a fully remote role.

The opportunity

  • Execute security risk assessments end-to-end — scoping, data gathering, analysis, findings documentation, and communicating results to stakeholders — in alignment with program methodology set by leadership

  • Support the development and continuous refinement of risk assessment templates, workflows, and process guides that make the program consistent and scalable

  • Maintain risk registers and ensure identified risks are tracked accurately and progressing through mitigation, remediation, or acceptance workflows

  • Assist in building and maintaining Key Risk Indicators (KRI) tracking and risk reporting outputs, translating raw data into clear, well-structured deliverables for review by senior leadership

  • Partner with technical teams including Vulnerability Management, Application Security, and Blue Team to gather risk-relevant data and incorporate operational findings into assessment work

  • Identify opportunities to streamline and automate risk processes and bring those recommendations to program leadership for prioritization

  • Contribute to the documentation and upkeep of risk program standards, procedures, and guidance materials

  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams including Compliance, Internal Audit, Engineering, and Legal to ensure risk findings are well-contextualized and properly actioned

  • Support audit preparedness activities and risk-related reporting as directed by program leadership

What you bring

  • 5+ years of experience in information security risk management, cybersecurity governance, or GRC

  • Hands-on experience conducting risk assessments and owning findings documentation — not just supporting assessments, but running them

  • Strong working knowledge of risk management frameworks such as NIST CSF, ISO 27005, PCI DSS, or DoCRA

  • Demonstrated ability to build repeatable processes — you've taken something ad hoc and made it structured and scalable

  • Strong data analysis skills; able to clean, interpret, and present risk data clearly and accurately

  • Experience contributing to KRI tracking and risk reporting for internal stakeholder audiences

  • Familiarity with GRC tools such as AuditBoard, Archer, OneTrust, or ServiceNow GRC

  • Proficient in Google Workspace; SQL and/or Tableau experience a strong plus

  • Excellent written communication — your deliverables are clear, well-organized, and don't require heavy editing

  • Self-directed and comfortable operating in ambiguity; you take direction well and run with it

  • Bachelor's degree or above in IT, Cybersecurity, Business Administration, Engineering, or a related field

  • CISM, CRISC, or ISO 27001 credentials a plus; experience in fintech or regulated industries preferred

Please note, applicants are permitted to redact or remove information on their resume that identifies age, date of birth, or dates of attendance at or graduation from an educational institution.

We consider qualified applicants with criminal histories for employment on our team, assessing candidates in a manner consistent with the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies, from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups, use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

Treasury brings business banking and payments together on Stripe. We help businesses receive, store, send, and spend their money in one place — with faster access to funds, global money movement, and cards for everyday spending. Instead of stitching together banks, payment processors, and financial tools, businesses can manage their money where they already run their payments.

For design, this is an opportunity to rethink money management- an essential part of running a business. How might we make managing money feel effortless, help businesses operate across currencies and borders with confidence, and turn complex financial operations into intuitive, powerful experiences that give people more time to focus on building their businesses?

We’re looking for a design leader to help shape those answers. Our ambition is to build products that are powerful, well-crafted, and beautiful—bringing the quality and care of the best consumer experiences to business financial tools. You’ll lead a team defining new experiences from the ground up, navigating substantial ambiguity and regulatory complexity without losing sight of what makes a product exceptional.

What you’ll do

Responsibilities

  • Lead a design team focused on Treasury, shaping a compelling vision for a unified experience across business banking, payments, money movement, and spending
  • Translate complex financial capabilities into intuitive experiences that help businesses access their funds faster, manage cash flow, and operate globally with confidence
  • Guide zero-to-one work from early exploration through launch, helping the team turn open-ended problems into clear product direction and cohesive experiences
  • Set a high bar for craft and beauty, coaching designers to deliver exceptional interaction design, visual design, and thoughtful details that build confidence and trust
  • Partner closely with Product, Engineering, Legal, Compliance, Risk, and other stakeholders to find ambitious solutions within financial and regulatory constraints
  • Build and develop a team of designers, growing their skills, judgment, and careers while fostering a high-performance, customer-obsessed team culture
  • Inspire the team and align cross-functional leaders around a clear design vision, balancing long-term ambition with pragmatic progress and world-class excellence in what we ship

Who you are

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • Have 5+ years of people management experience and are confident in building and developing design teams in fast-paced, evolving environments.
  • Experience leading design teams tackling complex products with technical or financial systems, including shaping zero-to-one products from understanding user needs and defining the problem to establishing a product direction and bringing it to market. 
  • Strong design judgment and a track record of helping teams deliver world-class, consumer-grade experiences. Ability to make sophisticated products feel simple, coach designers toward outstanding interaction and visual craft, and balance detail-oriented design with big-picture strategy, combining a deep understanding of users with business goals to drive meaningful outcomes
  • Comfortable designing within regulatory constraints and partnering with legal, compliance, and risk teams. You can distinguish firm requirements from assumptions and find creative solutions without compromising user trust or regulatory obligations.
  • Have demonstrated the ability to drive progress through substantial ambiguity. You bring structure to unclear problems, make sound decisions with incomplete information, and help teams move forward as requirements evolve.
  • Excel at balancing detail-oriented design with big-picture strategy, combining a deep understanding of users with business goals to drive meaningful outcomes.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills, using storytelling and clear reasoning to align teams and influence senior stakeholders

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience designing financial products, particularly banking or bank-like experiences, money management, cards, or treasury tools.
  • Experience delivering products across global markets with differing regulatory, operational, and user needs.
  • Experience bringing fragmented tools and workflows together into a cohesive product experience with a consistently high standard of craft.

Hut 8 brings exceptional people together to solve the world’s most consequential problems at the intersection of energy and technology. Today, that means building infrastructure for AI at a pace and scale without precedent. Tomorrow, it could mean powering a new era of innovation through robotics, advanced manufacturing, or an industry that does not yet exist. Whatever the technology demands, our ambition holds: to build the defining physical infrastructure company of our generation.

We look for thinkers and builders with the rigor, humility, and ownership to solve problems at this scale. They start from zero and choose truth over tradition. They back the best idea, whatever its source. They bet on themselves and embrace the hard truths that force them to grow. Our commitment is to keep the path from idea to execution short, trust them with critical decisions and the work that follows, and surround them with colleagues whose curiosity extends beyond their expertise.

ABOUT THE ROLE

The Mechanical Systems Expert is Managed Services' expert embedded in a data center build - supporting design review and commissioning to ensure cooling systems are operable and maintainable at turnover. Every design decision eventually becomes someone's 3 a.m. problem; this role reviews the design and witnesses the testing on behalf of that person.


Some of the key responsibilities you should expect are the following:

Operability Design Review

Review mechanical and cooling designs - chilled water plants, air and liquid cooling systems, CDUs, CRAHs, heat rejection, water treatment - through an operations lens: maintenance access and laydown, isolation and redundancy behavior, degraded-mode operation, instrumentation adequacy, and failure-mode consequences. File review comments that change designs, not just document concerns.

Construction-Phase Verification

Walk mechanical installations at key milestones: pipe routing and support, valve access, equipment clearances, insulation quality, and cleanliness/flushing protocol compliance - catching operability problems while they're still cheap to fix.

Commissioning Witness

Witness Level 3-5 commissioning of mechanical systems: functional performance tests, staging and failover sequences, failure scenarios, and integrated systems testing. Drive operational issues into the Cx log with clear acceptance criteria and verify closure personally.

Turnover Readiness

Verify mechanical turnover packages: O&Ms, as-builts, valve tags and system labeling, water treatment baselines, spare parts and consumables lists, and PM program inputs (frequencies, procedures, vendor contacts). Validate training actually equips operators to run the plant.

Operations Transition Support

Support early operations stabilization post-turnover: alarm tuning input, setpoint refinement, and first-months troubleshooting alongside the operations team.

Program Feedback

Feed operational lessons into Hut 8 mechanical design standards and the next project's basis of design.

ABOUT YOU

What we're looking for:

  • 8+ years in critical facilities mechanical operations, commissioning, or chief-engineer-track roles.
  • Deep hands-on knowledge of chilled water plants, hydronic systems, and data center cooling topologies - air-cooled, water-cooled, and liquid/direct-to-chip.
  • Level 1-5 commissioning fluency from the witness/operations side, including integrated systems testing.
  • Sharp eye for maintainability in design reviews: access, isolation, and instrumentation gaps.
  • Turnover documentation rigor - you read the O&M before signing for it.
  • Comfortable embedded with a construction team while holding the operations line.
  • Water treatment and cleanliness protocol experience for critical hydronic systems.
  • CFC/EPA certifications, trade licensure, or engineering degree all welcome paths.

ABOUT THE WORK ENVIRONMENT

  • Full time on-site in St. Francisville, LA.

BitGo (NYSE: BTGO) is the digital asset infrastructure company delivering custody, wallets, staking, trading, financing, stablecoins, and settlement services from regulated cold storage. Since 2013, BitGo has focused on accelerating the transition of the financial system to a digital asset economy. BitGo maintains a global presence and multiple regulated entities, including BitGo Bank & Trust, National Association, the first federally chartered digital asset trust bank owned by a publicly traded company. Today, BitGo serves thousands of institutions, including many of the industry's top brands, financial institutions, exchanges, and platforms, and millions of investors worldwide. For more information, visit www.bitgo.com.

This role will require being full-time onsite at our Palo Alto office to support collaborative team dynamics and innovative problem-solving.

BitGo is looking for a design leader who still designs. You will manage and mentor the design team, own the design system, and sit next to the Chief Product Officer on business strategy.

This is a player-coach role, and we mean it literally. You will carry your own design surfaces and ship them, alongside leading the team. Expect roughly 50% hands-on IC work to start, decreasing as the team scales. It will not go to zero — the person setting the craft bar should be practicing at it.

We are not a design-forward company today. We intend to become one, and we want you to lead that shift.

The team you will lead

The design team is small, senior, and self-sufficient. Each designer owns a wide vertical outright — trading, staking, DeFi vaults, earn, wallets, financing — with deep product context and strong opinions about the work. They are running at capacity, which is part of why this role carries real IC load: you will pick up the retail mobile experience and design system rather than distributing that work across a team that is already full.

What they have asked for is specific, and we are hiring against it: a leader who gets into the work early with product and engineering rather than arriving at the end, who can critique craft because they still practice it, who tells them plainly what the next level requires, and who gives the team air cover so they can do the deep work instead of patching to hit dates.

What you will own

  • Your own design work. You will own surfaces directly and ship them at the quality bar you are asking of everyone else. Discovery through spec, in Figma, in the reviews, on the hard problems.
  • The team's growth. Invest in each designer individually. Be explicit about what the next level requires and give people the work that gets them there. Feedback should be candid, specific, and about the craft. Respect the ownership designers already have — autonomy is how this team works best, and your job is to raise the ceiling, not take the pen.
  • Design's standing in the company. Amplify the team's visibility, voice, and strategic impact. Represent design in strategy, roadmap, and architecture conversations, and push for the client experience when nobody else in the room will.
  • Upstream involvement. Join product and engineering at discovery, not at handoff. Shape long-term roadmaps with PMs so the team builds toward a direction instead of absorbing late changes.
  • The design system. Own the system and component library end to end: tokens, patterns, governance, contribution model, and adoption across product teams. Translate company strategy into a system flexible enough that teams ship scalable experiences rather than one-off patches.
  • Systems design. Our platform spans seven product areas with shared primitives — accounts, wallets, assets, entitlements, approvals. Design the system, not the screen.
  • The discipline. Establish UX and systems thinking as a practice the whole organization runs on, not a stage a design team owns. Product managers, engineers, and business leads should be able to frame a client problem, map the system it lives in, and evaluate a solution against real client needs. That is how we ship value to every client type we serve, in every market we operate in — rather than a set of features that work for the loudest account.
  • How we work. Establish the processes a small team needs to move fast without losing quality: critique, documentation, design review, and clean handoffs with engineering. Set the quality bar and hold it, including for AI-assisted work.
  • Technical depth. Read a technical design, understand the constraint, and decide with engineering where to compromise, where to hold, and where a broader change is worth the cost. Get into the mechanics with the team on the hard edge cases — the crypto ones and the design ones.
  • The face of design. Be present and known internally, and represent BitGo design externally with clients, partners, and candidates.

What success looks like

By six months: the design system has a clear owner, a versioned component library, and measurable adoption. Product teams stop reinventing patterns. You have shipped design work of your own that the team points to as the standard. Every designer knows what their next level requires and has work that supports getting there.

By 12 months: design is in the room early on strategy, not late on execution. Product and engineering partners frame problems in client terms without being asked. The team has grown in size and capability. At least one flagship surface has shipped with a coherent, systemized experience clients notice.

Who you are

  • Experience leading design in financial services. Digital assets, or another domain of genuinely complex technical flows, strongly preferred.
  • You have built and owned a design system at scale, not just used one.
  • Hands-on in Figma and a role model for craft. You are shipping design work today, not describing work you shipped four years ago. You can sit in a critique and give feedback that is specific enough to act on.
  • Deep in UX. Strong product thinking, logical reasoning, and decisions grounded in data rather than taste alone.
  • You have managed designers and made them better. You care about how the team is doing, not only what it ships.
  • Technically literate. Comfortable with APIs, data models, and engineering trade-offs.
  • Direct communicator. You can hold a position with a Chief Product Officer, an engineering lead, or a client, and change your mind when the argument is better.
  • You want the mandate. Turning a technical, compliance-heavy platform into a design-led one is the appeal, not the obstacle.

Helpful, not required

  • Regulated environments: broker-dealer, trust company, bank, or qualified custodian.
  • Experience with complex permissioning, approval workflows, or multi-entity account structures.
  • Design leadership at a company that went through the same shift you would lead here.

Why Join BitGo?

Disrupting an industry takes vision, innovation, passion, technical chops, drive to deliver, collaboration, and execution. Join a team of great people who strive for excellence and personify our corporate values of ownership, craftsmanship, and open communication. We are looking for new colleagues who bring innovative ways of thinking and problem-solving, and who want risks to be part of the team that changes the world’s financial markets.

  • 100% company-paid health insurance for employee, partner, and dependents

Pay Transparency Notice:

Depending upon your leveling and location, the compensation for this role averages between $210,000 and $250,000 USD base salary. Equity, an annual performance bonus, and the benefits outlined above are also part of this role’s package.

Ondo Finance is looking for a Senior Product Designer to own, hands-on, the design systems behind everything we ship. You'll own two outright, institutional and consumer, and support the marketing team's system so brand and design-to-code stay tight. Our products move real money, so precision and accessibility are the floor, not the ceiling: we want institutional and consumer users alike to feel the craft, which makes visual expression and motion core to the system. You'll join a small, senior team that runs on high ownership and low ego, and this is a building role: you'll be in Figma and alongside engineers every day, shipping the components and tokens yourself while setting the direction for the systems you own.

Target Outcomes
  • Both design systems, institutional and consumer, fully adopted across their web and mobile products, with measurable coverage (share of screens built from system components) rising quarter over quarter.
  • Figma libraries and the front-end component library in parity: tokens, variants, and states match one-to-one, with drift caught and resolved as part of normal release cadence.
  • Every system component meets WCAG AA, with accessibility criteria documented and verified before release, and the systems carry a visual and motion language that users notice and teams can reuse.
  • Product teams ship faster: fewer one-off components, shorter design-to-build cycles, and a clear contribution path that teams actually use.
  • Documentation and governance that scale beyond the design team: engineers, PMs, and AI agents can build correctly from the system without a designer in the loop.
Responsibilities
  • Own two design systems end to end, institutional and consumer: components, design tokens, theming, patterns, and the Figma libraries behind them, across web and mobile. Support the marketing team's design system as needed so brand practice stays consistent and design-to-code stays smooth.
  • Define the expressive layer of both systems: visual language, motion principles, and the interaction details that make institutional and consumer products feel considered and alive, not merely correct.
  • Design and ship the full stack of the system, from primitives and atoms through molecules and organisms to page templates, with polished interaction details and the visual hierarchy, typography, and layout rigor that trading and financial interfaces demand.
  • Partner closely with UI engineers so that tokens and components map cleanly to the production component library, and so Figma and code stay in sync.
  • Define how the system works on mobile: platform-appropriate interactions, responsive and adaptive behavior, and parity rules between web and native surfaces.

  • Write clear, usable documentation (usage guidelines, do/don't examples, contribution guides) that designers, engineers, and AI agents can all work from.
  • Run governance across teams: contribution and review process, versioning and deprecation, adoption tracking, and the forums where product teams propose and resolve system changes.
  • Audit the system proactively to find gaps, inconsistencies, and drift across products, then prioritize and drive the fixes without waiting to be asked.
  • Use AI tooling as part of daily work: agents, markdown guideline files, and MCP integrations that connect the design system to design and engineering workflows.
Requirements
  • 6+ years in product design, including 3+ years focused on design systems.
  • Experience building and scaling a shared design system across multiple products and platforms, web and mobile, including mobile-specific design systems and interactions.
  • Strong UI craft: visual hierarchy, typography, layout, and polished interaction details, with a point of view on motion and visual expression and the taste to know when restraint is the right call.
  • Builds scalable components and design tokens, including theming (for example light/dark modes or multi-brand).
  • A strong understanding of how components and tokens translate into front-end libraries: how components are built, composed, and consumed in code (for example React, React Native, or Swift/Kotlin component libraries), and how tokens flow from Figma into code.
  • Advanced Figma skills: variables and modes, auto layout, component properties, and library management at scale.
  • A track record of working closely with engineers as a day-to-day partner, not a handoff.
  • Strong accessibility knowledge and experience shipping WCAG AA compliant components.
  • Writes clear documentation and has run governance across teams: contribution models, review processes, and adoption.
  • Fluency with AI tooling in a design or engineering workflow: using agents, writing markdown guideline files, and working with MCP integrations.
  • Experience with design-to-code tooling such as Code Connect, token pipelines, or Storybook.
  • A systems thinker with sharp attention to detail who sees both the pattern and the pixel.
  • A portfolio that showcases design systems work: components, tokens, documentation, and the reasoning behind the decisions.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with crypto, onchain or tokenized-asset products.
  • Experience in fintech, exchanges, or trading platforms. Design systems for trading surfaces have their own nuances: dense data tables, real-time state changes, numeric typography, and color semantics for gains, losses, and risk.
  • Familiarity with crypto and digital-asset products, or with tokenized assets and markets.
  • Experience setting up motion and interaction standards within a system.
  • Working proficiency in Mandarin Chinese.
What we offer
  • Competitive compensation including but not limited to salary, future token rights, and/or equity (according to your preferences) — We are well-funded and believe that great talent deserves great compensation.
  • Full benefits (medical, vision, and dental) and flexible vacation policy (PTO).

Application Instructions

Interviewing with TRM

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while allowing you to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, an AI skills assessment, and a Leadership Principles interview.

  • Structure and solve problems

  • Improve output quality

  • Increase speed and leverage

  • A high level of personal ownership and accountability

  • Frequent, high-touch communication

  • Creative problem-solving and out-of-the-box thinking

About the job

About HIFI

HIFI is a stablecoin infrastructure company building technology for the next-generation of financial products. We build tools for payments and tokenized money products across money movement, cards, and capital markets. Institutions and enterprises already use our platform and APIs to move billions of dollars in production environments around the world, and we are still early.

 

Founded in 2022, our organization is flat and our team is talent dense. We work in person at our office in Flatiron and are intentional about who we work with. We've raised $37 million from world-class investors, including a Series A led by Left Lane Capital.

 

About the Team

HIFI's compliance team is what makes it possible for banks, fintechs, and institutions to move money on stablecoin rails with confidence. The team owns the BSA/AML program, sanctions controls, and client onboarding that every partnership and every dollar of volume depends on. As stablecoin regulation takes shape this role helps HIFI scales from an early-stage startup into a long-term, category-defining platform, this team will set the standard for how compliance is built into institutional stablecoin infrastructure, as a core part of the product rather than an add-on.

 

The Head of Financial Crime Compliance owns that effort day to day. You'll run HIFI's BSA/AML and sanctions program across both fiat and on-chain flows, and you'll be the primary point of contact for banking partners, auditors, and examiners. This is a senior role with real ownership: you'll set policy, manage and grow the compliance team, and work directly with product and engineering to turn regulatory requirements into onboarding flows and monitoring rules.

 

Responsibilities

  • Own HIFI's BSA/AML and sanctions compliance program across fiat and stablecoin flows, including the annual risk assessment and independent testing.

  • Oversee KYC/KYB and enhanced due diligence for institutional clients, fintechs, and financial institutions, and make final calls on high-risk onboarding decisions.

  • Manage transaction monitoring and investigations, including alert quality, escalation standards, and final review and filing of SARs.

  • Run sanctions screening (OFAC and other applicable lists) on clients, counterparties, and blockchain wallet addresses, and set the standards for resolving potential matches.

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for banking partners, auditors, and examiners, and own responses to diligence requests and exam findings.

  • Write and maintain compliance policies and procedures, including stablecoin-specific requirements under the GENIUS Act, and brief leadership on regulatory changes that affect the business.

  • Partner with product and engineering to design onboarding flows, monitoring rules, and system controls, and evaluate and select compliance vendors and tooling.

  • Hire, manage, and develop the compliance team, and set the processes that let the function scale with transaction volume.

 

You might be a fit if

  • 7+ years of relevant experience in BSA/AML, financial crime compliance, payments compliance, fintech compliance, banking, crypto, or a related field.

  • Experience operating at a senior individual contributor or management level within a regulated financial services, payments, fintech, crypto, or banking environment.

  • Strong working knowledge of BSA/AML, KYC/KYB, customer due diligence, enhanced due diligence, OFAC sanctions, transaction monitoring, and suspicious activity escalation.

  • Strong understanding of payment flows, including ACH, wire, RTP, cross-border payments, virtual accounts, and other bank payment rails.

  • Strong familiarity with stablecoins, digital asset transactions, blockchain-based settlement, wallets, and crypto compliance risks.

  • Experience working with compliance platforms such as Sumsub, Persona, TRM Labs, Chainalysis, or similar systems.

  • Demonstrated experience improving or redesigning manual compliance processes through automation, workflow design, tooling, or operational controls.

  • Strong judgment and the ability to distinguish between regulatory requirements, partner requirements, internal policy, and risk-based business decisions.

  • Ability to communicate complex compliance issues clearly to technical, operational, commercial, and executive stakeholders.

  • Strong project management skills and the ability to drive remediation and implementation work across multiple teams.

  • Comfort operating in a fast-moving environment where products, regulations, counterparties, and risk profiles evolve quickly.

 

Why This Role Matters

Every institution that moves money on HIFI's rails is trusting that the compliance behind them is airtight. This is a chance to build that trust from the ground up at a stablecoin payments infrastructure company as it scales, and to help set the standard for how compliance should work.

 

Additional Requirement

Must be within a commutable distance from our office and able to work in person most days of the week.
